moat_against: No switching costs; guests can trade down to fast-casual, QSR or home meals at any time
Pricing power limited by value competition — Chili's value resurgence pressures Olive Garden directly
Beef inflation at cyclical highs hits LongHorn, the fastest-growing brand; ~3.5% labor inflation guided for FY27
Olive Garden comps slowed to +1.0-1.1% in Q1 FY27; younger-guest softness flagged by management
Mature US casual-dining market: underlying unit and comp growth is low-single-digit
moat_for: Scale: largest US full-service operator (~2,200 restaurants) — purchasing, talent and data advantages
Anchor brands Olive Garden and LongHorn with long positive-comp records; LongHorn +6.2-6.8% comps in Q1 FY27
Diversified portfolio across casual, steakhouse and fine dining dampens single-concept slumps
Disciplined capital return: buybacks shrinking share count ~1.8%/yr, dividend raised 8% in June 2026
Proven through-cycle operator: owner's earnings positive 5 of last 5 fiscal years
moat_justification: Moderate/narrow moat (5/10): the largest US full-service operator with genuine scale in purchasing, talent and data, and two proven anchor brands (Olive Garden, LongHorn Steakhouse) that have compounded same-restaurant sales through cycles — LongHorn posted its 22nd consecutive positive-comp quarter in Q1 FY27. But restaurants have no switching costs, pricing power is capped by consumer elasticity and value rivals (Brinker's Chili's, Texas Roadhouse, fast-casual), and returns depend on re-earning traffic every quarter against beef and labor inflation. That earns a mid-range fade, not a wide-moat one: CAP = 8.5 years.
name: Darden Restaurants, Inc.
one_liner: High-quality, narrow-moat restaurant operator (moat 5/10) that does not come close to the 15% hurdle at $214.28 — weighted IRR 7.07%, weighted IV@15% $76.50; it would need to fall to about $76.50 to clear 15% on these inputs.
